most_effective_hook_patterns: Credibility-plus-doom: former insider + reluctance signal + specific scary claim
Dystopian irony: company/institution admits danger while asking for money/trust
Numbers that shouldn't exist: stack 3 absurd real figures, one-word kicker
Leaked-reality-vs-belief: surface the gap between trusted public number and actual leaked figure
Live-crisis-as-thesis-proof: real-time event that vindicates a long-marginalized view
Historical enumeration + contrarian reframe: list past fears, current fear is last, punchy kicker closes
Hidden-danger-in-trusted-product: visual proof of something that shouldn't be inside a trusted device
Meta-contrarian reframe: the viral warning is actually a marketing move — I can see it, can you?
most_effective_formats: Educational thread with a numbered breakdown (5-8 tweets)
Single dry/ironic tweet under 140 chars with no hashtags
Product launch in 3 sentences (social proof → reveal → competitor dismissal)
Math thread: open with headline, prove the bear case with real numbers
Insider-voice thread with credibility in tweet 1, evidence in tweets 2-5
Tweet + image comparison (side-by-side mockery or proof)
Whistleblower essay-thread: resignation + sacrifice signal + insider claim chain
most_effective_tones: Darkly humorous / dry — irony without explanation
Authoritative-alarmed — factual tone on scary content
Confident-dismissive — short, no hedge, implicit superiority
Vulnerable-credentialed — admitting something against self-interest from a position of authority
Alarmed-analytical — physical evidence + measured explanation (trust collapse content)
Meta-knowing — second-order cynicism, spoken from above the fray
most_effective_triggers: Fear of AI autonomy / loss of control
FOMO on a next-gen founder's trajectory
Intellectual superiority (I see what others miss)
Physical evidence shock (hardware implant, leaked doc, screenshot)
Supply-chain paranoia (my trusted hardware/software was compromised)
Participatory mockery (I can join this wave and add my own example)
cross_niche_insights: The highest-reach AI posts combine insider credibility + reluctance to share + specific scary claim — this triple-stack is the dominant virality template in AI discourse in 2026
Dry irony outperforms earnest outrage: one-sentence juxtapositions of dystopian facts get more engagement than multi-paragraph rants
Crypto content is migrating toward meta-commentary (about the platform, the regulators, the suppression) rather than price/project content — the grievance IS the content
Second-order takes on mega-viral posts (reframing the motive behind a viral claim) now generate their own viral cycle — the contrarian response to a 100M-view post is itself a high-reach format
Physical/visual proof is the ultimate engagement catalyst across both AI and crypto: hardware implant photos, side-by-side comparisons, screenshots from leaked docs — images short-circuit skepticism
Teen/young founder adversity-to-success threads spike engagement when the rejection count is extreme and specific — the institutional gatekeeping itself becomes the villain

Creator-kills-their-own-creation announcements generate disproportionate engagement in developer/tech communities due to community identity investment — the more beloved the project, the higher the reach
